requirements.requirement: Publish node4's HTTP service (port 8080 on lan-b) on TCP port 80 of node2's transit address
requirements.summary: node2's transit interface (opt1/vtnet1) was assigned 10.10.2.2/30, and a destination-NAT (rdr) rule was added redirecting TRANSIT:80 to node4's lan-b address (10.10.3.2:8080), with matching pf pass rules. After debugging two pf issues (a self-IP macro resolution bug and post-NAT vs pre-NAT rule matching), curl from node1 and node3 to http://10.10.2.2:80/ returned HTTP 200 with node4's page content, directly confirming the publish worked end-to-end.

requirements.requirement: Give node1 a route to node2's transit address
requirements.summary: node1 (VyOS) eth1 was configured with 10.10.2.1/30 via 'configure/commit/save', placing node1 directly on the same transit subnet as node2's 10.10.2.2 address, giving it a connected route. Verified with 'ip -4 addr show eth1' output and later successful curl to 10.10.2.2:80 confirming reachability.

requirements.requirement: node3 on lan-a reaches the service by asking node2 rather than addressing node4 directly
requirements.summary: node3 was configured with a static IP (10.10.1.2/30) and a route to 10.10.0.0/16 via node1 (its only path toward the transit/lan-b networks). node3 has no interface or route to node4's lan-b subnet (10.10.3.0/30), so its successful curl to http://10.10.2.2:80/ (node2's transit address) necessarily traverses node2, not node4 directly. This was verified again after all four node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node1 baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 01e92881... captured, reboot triggered via nohup reboot, connection loss/timeouts observed during the transition, and a new boot_id 4d1eed11... confirmed afterward. Post-restart checks show eth1/eth2 addresses, ip_forward, and a successful curl to the published service, all recovered. Cross-checked against the fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot, which shows the same new boot_id.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node2 baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline kern.boottime 04:22:28 captured, reboot issued via shutdown -r now, and a new boottime of 04:44:24 (uptime '1 min') confirmed the restart. Post-restart checks show opt1/opt2 interface addresses, the static route, and the NAT rdr rule all persisted in config.xml, and a curl from node2 to node4 succeeded, demonstrating full recovery. Matches the fixed after-executor snapshot's boot-identity.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node3 baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 9bdcc129... captured, reboot issued, connection loss observed, and new boot_id 15330935... confirmed. Post-restart checks show the nmcli-persisted static IP/route intact and a successful curl to the published service (200), confirming recovery. Matches the fixed after-executor snapshot's boot-identity.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node4 baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id f54d7366... captured, reboot issued, connection loss observed, and new boot_id 76a4217f... confirmed. Post-restart checks show the systemd service active, the firewalld port persisted, and localhost curl returning 200; a final cross-node curl (node3->node2->node4) also succeeded after all four restarts, confirming full end-to-end recovery. Matches the fixed after-executor snapshot's boot-identity.

overall_summary: All three material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence: node2's transit address (10.10.2.2:80) now dest-NATs to node4's service (10.10.3.2:8080), node1 was given connectivity to that transit address via a directly-connected VyOS interface, and node3 was shown to reach the service exclusively through node2 (it has no route/interface to node4's lan-b subnet). The mandatory provider-wide restart protocol was executed and fully evidenced for all four nodes, each showing a genuine baseline-to-post-restart boot-identity change followed by re-verified healthy/recovered state, and these boot identities are corroborated by the fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot. Hygiene is good but not perfect: several bounded, fully-reverted temporary IP-addressing experiments were used for topology discovery when read-only tools likely would have sufficed, though they left no residue and posed no risk.
limitations: The claim that node4's lan-b address is unreachable from node3/node1 is inferred from the observed routing/interface configuration rather than from a captured direct negative-reachability test (e.g., a failed curl from node3 to 10.10.3.2).

Some restart-protocol timeline commands (e.g., intermediate timeout/connection-reset probes) are omitted from the cited evidence for brevity but are consistent with the cited baseline/post-restart pairs.

Package-health and failed-service checks for node2 (OPNsense) are marked 'unsupported' in the lifecycle snapshots since it lacks systemd/dpkg equivalents, so hygiene for that node relies on pf/NAT/interface state comparisons rather than a native health check.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor ran several bounded topology-discovery experiments that mutated interface addressing beyond read-only diagnostics, all of which were fully reverted with no residue confirmed in the after-executor snapshot: (1) temporary link-local 169.254.99.1/24 and 172.31.99.1/30 addresses added and immediately deleted within the same command on node1/node3/node4 for arping-based link mapping (cmd-a507e92bdac349e8, cmd-edc8e076e54d47df, cmd-3918995c3b88462c); (2) a broader temporary 172.31.50.0/24 addressing scheme applied to all four nodes' inter-node interfaces to ping-test the mesh (cmd-e1583906c12d43ef, cmd-f206e16f4f1e4668, cmd-eb657753b25f4d06, cmd-2c3d34c9b6e94b81), later fully removed (cmd-f5a33ae8eb6c4793, cmd-3cafb67d2dec4831, cmd-b85c741f0b9046b7, cmd-0c7f32f28bcc483d). These were low-risk, private-range, bounded mutations with no lasting effect, but they were not strictly necessary since the topology was already derivable from ip/ARP read-only inspection. Extensive tcpdump/pfctl troubleshooting during the NAT/pf debugging was read-only or self-cleaning (processes killed, temp log files left under /tmp are inconsequential and consistent with normal OS churn). No failed services, no unremediated address/config drift, and no security-control weakening were found in the after-executor lifecycle comparison.
